Part of #377

## Question

Does the record need a predicate saying whether the object in hand is a SQL
query, and if so is `is_sql_lazy_query()` extracted out of what
`grouping_backend()` computes inline at `R/grouping-backend.R:14`?

The map's fog listed this as "a judgement that rides on whichever features
survive". They have all now been decided — #381 rejected the condition, #382
rejected `"explain"`, #383 fixed `last_sent_queries()` and the reset in
`prepare_grouping_plan()`, #384 rejected the on-disk log — so the question has a
subject and can be put.

What has to be decided:

1. **Whether the record needs the predicate at all.** #318's warrant for it was
   "self-detection from the query object means no call site needs to thread
   backend/operation through just for this" — an argument about the
   `signal_marginplyr_query_sql()` helper, which #381 removed. #383 put the
   reset in `prepare_grouping_plan()`, where `grouping_backend()` has already
   run, so the sites may be *handed* the kind rather than recomputing it. ADR
   0020's predicate for whether a query is sent is `is.data.frame()`, not a SQL
   test, and #383 recorded that `grouping_selection_proxy()` sends nothing on
   arrow and nothing on a backend without `collect_selection_proxy` — neither of
   which a `tbl_lazy` test answers.
2. **If it is needed, whether extraction is the shape.** #378 answered the
   mechanics and they cut against it: `is_dtplyr` and `is_arrow` are locals
   `grouping_backend()` computes for its own `kind` cascade whether or not
   `is_sql` moves, so extracting buys no arithmetic; and the helper must call
   `arrow_input_classes()` rather than spell the vector, since that function's
   header says it exists *because* a second copy of the vector is what would
   drift (`R/grouping-backend.R:1-8`).
3. **Whether it stands on its own merits regardless.** #318 concedes
   `grouping_backend()` needs no helper for its own sake. If the record does not
   need one either, #318's section is deleted rather than kept, and that is the
   answer.

The map's *Out of scope* rules out writing the R code. What this decides is
whether the specification #385 assembles contains the helper at all.

## Resolution

A verdict, and — if the helper survives — the contract its header would state,
so #385 can write it into #318 rather than re-deciding it.
title: Decide whether the record needs a SQL-detection predicate

body:
## Summary

#430 names an unnamed summary marginplyr rewrites, from the expression the
caller wrote. dplyr expands a data-frame-valued summary's columns into the
result only while that summary is unnamed, and packs them into one column under
any name. So a data-frame-valued summary a rewrite reaches now comes back
packed where it used to expand.

`name_rewritten_summary_dots()` (`R/summary-selections.R`) excludes the two
data-frame-valued shapes a static reading recognizes — a summary written as
`across()` or `pick()` itself, and the `tibble()`/`data.frame()` family. What is
left is a data-frame-valued expression the reading does not recognize.

## Reproduction

```r
pkgload::load_all(".", quiet = TRUE)
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))

data <- data.frame(group = c("a", "a", "b"), x = c(1, 3, 5), y = c(2, 4, 6))
range_frame <- function(columns) data.frame(lo = min(columns[[1L]]), hi = max(columns[[1L]]))
totals <- function(value, bit) data.frame(sum = sum(value), margin = bit)

names(summarize(data, range_frame(pick(x)), .by = group))
#> [1] "group" "lo"    "hi"

names(summarize_with_margins(data, range_frame(pick(x)), .grouping = rollup(group)))
#> [1] "group"                       "range_frame(dplyr::pick(x))"

names(summarize_with_margins(data, totals(x, grouping_bit(group)), .grouping = rollup(group)))
#> [1] "group"                          "totals(x, grouping_bit(group))"
```

A summary no rewrite reaches — `range_frame(x)` — expands as before, and so
does `across(c(x, y), mean)`.

`tests/testthat/test-grouping-interface.R`'s *a rewritten data-frame-valued
summary is named and packed* asserts both shapes above, so this is pinned
rather than latent.

## Why #430 did not fix it

Which of two expressions is data-frame-valued is a question about the value's
type, and the two are one call apart: `nrow(pick(v, w))` has to be named, which
is #430's second reproduction, while `range_frame(pick(x))` has to not be.
ADR 0019 reads spellings statically, and no static reading separates them.

#430's own *Fix direction* — `rlang::quos_auto_name()` applied before any
rewriting — packs strictly more than this, `across()` and `range_frame(x)`
included. What shipped is the narrower rule.

## What a fix would need

Deciding after the summarize rather than before: name the dot, and where a
branch result holds a data-frame column under a name marginplyr assigned,
expand it there. It needs the set of assigned names carried to the adapters
beside the dots and the labels `new_summary_arguments()` already carries, and
`check_summary_output_names()` run after the expansion rather than before.

ADR 0020 is not engaged if the check is confined to a local data frame, which
is the only input that reached this at all — dtplyr, Arrow, and the SQL
backends each refuse a data-frame-valued summary built from a function of the
caller's own, by their own errors, before and after #430.

## What is unmeasured

- Whether any backend other than a local data frame can hold a packed
  data-frame column, which decides whether the expansion above needs a backend
  capability or only an `is.data.frame()` guard.
- What `check_summary_output_names()` and `check_margin_id_collision()` would
  report for a marginplyr-assigned name that collides, which today can only
  happen for a name no caller wrote.
title: A rewritten data-frame-valued summary is named, so dplyr packs what it used to expand

body:
## Problem Statement

marginplyr is preparing its first CRAN release, but a green check in a fully
provisioned development environment currently hides several correctness,
specification, documentation, and release-engineering gaps. The most serious
defects affect Parent shares: displayed Margin labels can corrupt local
cardinality matching for non-character dimensions, dtplyr can silently coerce
an ineligible source or produce Cartesian rows for a non-scalar source, and
Arrow cannot preserve the package's targeted condition contract through its
native execution bridge. The current implementation also evaluates
`.grouping` through two paths, degrades some required `across()` diagnostics,
infers package errors from third-party message text, and repeatedly scans local
input during cardinality validation.

The package is also not robust when Suggested packages are absent. A
dependency-only check fails in examples, tests, and vignettes because optional
packages are used without complete guards. User documentation, release
metadata, architecture documentation, and tests contain smaller gaps or
duplicated sources of truth. The maintainer does not want to submit on a
deadline or treat version number as a proxy for progress: every review finding
must be verified and either fixed or explicitly rejected with evidence, and a
fresh review must have no unresolved Standards, Spec, or Docs & Tests findings
before submission.

## Solution

Harden the existing 0.1.0 interface without adding new public features.
Preserve the documented Margin and Parent-share contracts, deepen Parent-share
execution behind one private interface, and select explicit local, general-
dbplyr, and lazy-non-SQL adapters from prepared backend metadata. Local and
dtplyr execution will enforce eligible type and scalar cardinality without
displayed-label identity, extra lazy queries, or implicit collection. Arrow
will reject only `share_of_parent()` with a targeted package error before query
construction until Arrow can preserve the complete lazy validation and
condition contract; other Arrow Margin operations remain supported. General
dbplyr retains its documented execution-time limitation.

Introduce a stable `marginplyr_error` base condition for errors created by the
package, replace message-text classification with structured conditions,
restore the specified `across()` diagnostics, and keep user/backend errors
intact. Make function references the canonical user contract, use vignettes
for explanation, condition every Suggested dependency, and establish
dependency-only plus full-backend release gates. Keep the first CRAN version at
0.1.0 and do not submit until implementation, documentation, verification, and
a new code review are all clean.

## User Stories

1. As a local data-frame user, I want Parent shares to work with integer grouping dimensions and the default Margin label, so that display formatting cannot break a valid calculation.
2. As a local data-frame user, I want Parent shares to work with double, logical, Date, factor, and character grouping dimensions according to their documented contracts, so that grouping-key storage type does not change correctness.
3. As a user with genuine missing grouping values, I want those values to remain distinct from omitted dimensions bearing a Margin label, so that each row reaches its correct rollup parent.
4. As a user choosing `.margin_label = NULL`, I want typed missing Margin values and Parent identity to remain independent, so that presentation choices never become structural keys.
5. As a user with adversarial column names, I want package-internal names to be collision-safe, so that names resembling implementation temporaries cannot corrupt results.
6. As a user of duplicate Grouping-set occurrences, I want every occurrence retained under the documented policy while parent lookup skips identical occurrences, so that result identity and Parent share semantics stay consistent.
7. As a user of fixed `.by` groups, I want Parent shares calculated independently within each fixed partition, including missing fixed keys, so that denominators never cross partitions.
8. As a user of an empty input, I want root and partitioned-empty behavior to retain the documented row count and double Parent-share type, so that empty pipelines remain type-stable.
9. As a user with a missing numerator, missing denominator, zero denominator, or local `NaN`, I want the documented missing result, so that edge cases are portable and predictable.
10. As a user with negative or greater-than-one ratios, I want finite Parent shares left unclamped, so that marginplyr does not impose presentation policy.
11. As a user writing an integer or double scalar summary, I want Parent shares returned as doubles, so that integer division cannot alter the result.
12. As a user writing a logical, date-time, duration, character, factor, list, or other ineligible source summary, I want a targeted error when the backend can enforce it, so that implicit coercion never masquerades as a valid share.
13. As a user writing a zero-length or multi-value source summary, I want a targeted scalar-cardinality error, so that missing or Cartesian grouping rows are never returned.
14. As a dtplyr user, I want valid Parent-share queries to remain native lazy steps until explicit execution, so that marginplyr does not materialize data behind my back.
15. As a dtplyr user, I want invalid source type and cardinality detected during explicit execution before an invalid group row is emitted, so that lazy behavior remains safe.
16. As an Arrow user, I want ordinary Margin summaries to remain supported even when Parent shares are temporarily unavailable, so that one unsupported helper does not disable the backend.
17. As an Arrow user requesting a Parent share, I want a targeted package error before an Arrow query is constructed, so that I never receive a wrong result, an implicit collection, or a generic bridge error.
18. As a general dbplyr user, I want Parent-share queries to remain lazy without validation-only schema or cardinality probes, so that database execution behavior remains explicit.
19. As a general dbplyr user, I want statically detectable Parent-share syntax and dependency errors reported before execution, so that the documented lazy limitation is not broader than necessary.
20. As a user supplying `.grouping` from my calling environment, I want it captured and evaluated exactly once with its original environment, so that Parent shares do not change tidy-evaluation behavior.
21. As a user selecting preceding summaries with `across()`, I want every documented name-based tidyselect form to work, so that Parent-share selection behaves consistently.
22. As a user selecting a duplicated summary name, I want an error explaining that the name was defined more than once, so that an existing column is not misleadingly reported as absent.
23. As a user selecting an unknown name, I want it distinguished from a forbidden type predicate, so that the corrective guidance matches the mistake.
24. As a user with a function-valued symbol in my environment, I want that symbol treated according to the documented selection grammar rather than automatically as `where()`, so that caller state cannot change diagnostics accidentally.
25. As a user whose summary expression raises an error containing words such as “Can't recycle,” I want the original condition propagated, so that marginplyr does not fabricate a Parent-share diagnosis.
26. As an R programmer, I want package-generated errors to inherit from `marginplyr_error`, so that I can handle them without matching English message text.
27. As an R programmer, I want backend and user-expression conditions left in their original classes, so that package error handling does not erase useful provenance.
28. As a user reading an important diagnostic, I want it to identify the cause, relevant names, and supported rewrite, so that the error is actionable.
29. As a package maintainer, I want important diagnostics protected from accidental degradation without treating punctuation and line wrapping as permanent compatibility promises, so that wording can improve safely.
30. As a CRAN checker without Suggested packages installed, I want examples, tests, and vignettes to complete or skip conditionally, so that optional dependencies are genuinely optional.
31. As a vignette reader without DuckDB, RSQLite, dtplyr, Arrow, knitr, or related tooling installed, I want optional sections skipped cleanly, so that documentation can still be rebuilt.
32. As a package maintainer, I want unused Suggested dependencies removed, so that installation and CRAN checks do not carry needless cost.
33. As a database user, I want at least one live portable SQLite fallback test and live DuckDB native and fallback tests, so that simulator SQL is backed by executed behavior.
34. As a dtplyr or Arrow user, I want supported backend claims backed by live end-to-end tests, so that a lazy class check alone cannot conceal incorrect collected rows.
35. As a documentation reader, I want function references to be the canonical source of user-visible rules, so that duplicated tables cannot drift.
36. As a vignette reader, I want narrative examples linked to the canonical reference instead of restating every contract, so that guides remain approachable and accurate.
37. As a user navigating related Margin functions and helpers, I want working cross-references and family links, so that no reference topic is a dead end.
38. As a package citer, I want citation title and year aligned with the released package metadata, so that generated citations identify the package correctly.
39. As a prospective user, I want NEWS to name the exported Parent-share and Grouping-plan inspection capabilities, so that the initial release is discoverable.
40. As a contributor, I want architecture documentation to describe the Parent-share module, its adapters, and current test seams, so that changes are made at the intended seam.
41. As a contributor, I want the glossary and ADRs to use one canonical term for each Grouping concept and to reflect current row-order semantics, so that documentation does not contradict implementation.
42. As a maintainer, I want local cardinality validation to avoid one full input rescan per Grouping set, so that validation does not scale unnecessarily with rollup depth.
43. As a maintainer, I want a benchmark that detects meaningful Parent-share regressions without putting timing assertions in CRAN tests, so that performance work remains evidence-based and portable.
44. As a release manager, I want dependency-only and fully provisioned check jobs, so that both optional-dependency hygiene and complete backend behavior are release gates.
45. As a release manager, I want checks run from the built source tarball on R release, devel, and oldrel, so that success does not depend on development-tree artifacts.
46. As a release manager, I want every review finding recorded as fixed or rejected with evidence, so that “review complete” has an auditable meaning.
47. As a release manager, I want a fresh Standards, Spec, and Docs & Tests review with no unresolved findings, so that the first CRAN submission reflects the finished package rather than a deadline.

## Implementation Decisions

- The release remains version 0.1.0. The work is pre-release stabilization of the first public contract, not a new feature release.
- The exported interface and existing Parent-share value semantics remain unchanged except that Arrow reports Parent shares as explicitly unsupported instead of returning or attempting an unsafe lazy query.
- `.by`, `.grouping`, and summary expressions are captured exactly once at the public verb. Parent-share admission must not evaluate and re-inject `.grouping`; validation uses the one prepared Grouping plan.
- One deep private Parent-share module owns request planning, parent mapping, type and cardinality validation, ratio calculation, internal-name cleanup, and backend dispatch. Its caller supplies the prepared Margin operation, staged ordinary-summary result, and planned requests.
- The backend seam is after ordinary Margin summaries are staged and before finalization. Adapter selection uses the prepared backend kind, not the result object's incidental class.
- There are three genuine Parent-share adapters: local, general dbplyr, and lazy non-SQL. Planner and adapter details remain private and do not enlarge the public interface.
- Every adapter identifies parents with the internal Grouping plan and Grouping set identifier. Displayed Margin labels and caller-visible `.id` values are never used as identity or raw/result join keys.
- All temporary names, including cardinality counters and parent keys, are allocated through the package's collision-safe internal-name mechanism.
- Local scalar validation is integrated with ordinary-summary execution or uses at most one auxiliary input pass. It does not reconstruct expected keys by rescanning the full input once per Grouping set.
- The dtplyr adapter wraps every ordinary source summary referenced by a Parent share in a private type-and-size validator. Prototype evidence shows that the wrapper remains a native lazy step, executes only during explicit collection, preserves valid local results, emits a package condition before an invalid row is emitted, and requires no validation-only query.
- The dtplyr validator receives source/output identity and the original public call as constants in the translated expression so execution-time conditions retain actionable names and call context. It must handle every referenced source without multiplying aggregations or parent mappings per measure.
- Arrow Parent shares use the targeted unsupported fallback. The fallback runs only after expression planning and normal locally detectable Margin-operation validation, but before ordinary summary execution constructs an Arrow query. Other Arrow Margin summaries remain supported.
- The Arrow decision follows prototype evidence for Arrow 25: schema inspection can reject some semantic types but cannot prove scalar cardinality; native UDF and batch hooks erase package condition subclasses and the original call; query wrappers are not preserved by important query-rebuilding verbs and would require message heuristics rejected by the condition contract.
- General dbplyr retains the documented relaxation: no additional result-type/cardinality query and no implicit collection. Static grammar and dependency errors stay targeted; incompatible runtime results may fail with a database condition.
- Package-created user-facing errors inherit from the stable `marginplyr_error` base class. More specific classes are introduced only for internal structured dispatch or a documented caller workflow; Parent-share cardinality uses a structured subclass.
- User-expression and backend conditions propagate unchanged. Rethrows and internal assertions are not mechanically reclassified.
- Human-facing diagnostics have a semantic contract: cause, relevant names, and actionable replacement. Exact punctuation, whitespace, and wrapping are not public compatibility guarantees.
- Parent-share execution catches structured package conditions, never regular-expression matches against condition messages.
- Parent-share `across()` planning retains candidate-name provenance instead of deleting duplicated or otherwise ineligible summaries from the selection context. Duplicate, unavailable, and unknown sources therefore remain distinguishable.
- Predicate detection follows the documented syntax and tidyselect forms rather than resolving arbitrary caller symbols to functions. Shared `across()` argument parsing is centralized instead of re-derived by Parent-share code.
- Repeated call-argument normalization, namespace checks, and duplicated user-facing diagnostics are consolidated only where doing so shrinks the internal interface and improves locality. New pass-through helpers are not introduced merely to reduce line count.
- Fragile local-state patterns are removed: initialize optional locals explicitly, replace side-effectful iteration with explicit ordered state, remove unused arguments and no-op expressions, and either use or remove unobserved internal condition markers.
- Parent-share implementation may be split into planner and adapter files for locality, but the conceptual module and its small interface remain one. File count and line count are not design goals.
- Suggested packages are guarded at every executable use in examples, tests, and vignettes. Tests use conditional skips; documentation chunks use explicit availability-driven evaluation. No optional package is promoted to Imports solely to make checks pass.
- Suggested packages with no remaining use are removed. Package metadata is reformatted and validated after edits.
- Function references are the canonical user-facing contract. Shared reference sections are inherited rather than copied. Vignettes explain workflows and link to the canonical contract; README and Get Started provide discovery and concise examples.
- Citation metadata, NEWS, related-function navigation, Quarto requirements, and CRAN comments are brought into alignment with the actual initial release.
- Architecture documentation is updated after the implementation to describe the current deep module, adapter seam, and test seams. Existing ADR statements that genuinely contradict current behavior are amended or superseded; defensible non-findings are not rewritten to satisfy a review mechanically.
- Every review observation receives a disposition in the implementation record: fixed with tests, or rejected with reproducible evidence. Claims already disproved by existing tests are not turned into redundant work.

## Testing Decisions

- The highest and primary test seam is the exported Margin verb interface, especially `summarize_with_margins()` with `share_of_parent()`. Good tests assert rows, columns, types, grouping, error classes and semantics, laziness, and collected results rather than private helper calls or list fields.
- The private Parent-share module is tested through the public interface. Focused internal tests are allowed only for a structured condition or adapter translation behavior that cannot be observed reliably at the higher seam.
- Existing Parent-share behavior tests are prior art for rollups, composite dimensions, fixed groups, duplicate occurrences, missing keys, empty input, multiple measures, and expression-order rules.
- Existing backend tests are prior art for dtplyr laziness, Arrow schema behavior, DuckDB native execution, portable SQL generation, missing-safe joins, and downstream query composition.
- Existing grouping-interface, Margin-label, Margin-id, factor, and summary-selection tests are prior art for Grouping plan identity, typed missing values, collision-safe names, column order, and grouped input.
- Add local regressions for default Margin labels with integer, double, logical, Date, factor, and character dimensions, plus an adversarial name matching the former hard-coded cardinality counter.
- Add local type/cardinality regressions for logical and semantic nonnumeric sources, zero-length summaries, two-value quantiles, local `NaN`, missing numerator, missing or zero denominator, and root behavior.
- Add dtplyr integration tests proving the result remains lazy before collection, valid integer/double results equal local output, invalid type and cardinality conditions appear only at explicit execution, original call context is retained, and no validation-only query is added.
- Add Arrow integration tests proving Parent shares fail at the agreed pre-query seam with a targeted `marginplyr_error`, no query or implicit collection occurs, and non-Parent-share Arrow Margin operations remain available.
- Add general dbplyr simulator tests for static validation and the documented runtime boundary, without pretending simulators can prove live execution.
- Add live RSQLite coverage for the portable `UNION ALL` path and retain live DuckDB comparison of native and forced-portable results. Simulator coverage remains useful for dialect query shape but does not substitute for these live tests.
- Add regressions showing an unrelated user/backend error containing recycling words is not reclassified, representative package errors inherit from `marginplyr_error`, and external conditions retain their original class.
- Add targeted diagnostic snapshots for Parent-share cardinality, duplicate source, unknown source, forbidden predicate, and unsupported Arrow behavior. Snapshots protect diagnostic meaning; they are not blanket coverage or a byte-for-byte public promise.
- Add exact behavior tests for `across()` duplicate, unavailable, unknown, and predicate cases, including a caller environment containing function-valued symbols.
- Add the previously identified secondary regressions for `nest_with_margins()` and `nest_by_with_margins()` with `.duplicates = "drop"`, documented `retail_sales` missing-store data, and any uncovered factor/NaN contract.
- Do not duplicate tests already covering contextual Grouping helpers outside Margin verbs or integer `.id` columns on zero-row results. Record those review claims as disproved by existing coverage.
- Benchmark representative local rollups before and after the cardinality redesign. Assert the removal of Grouping-set-proportional full input scans structurally; do not put wall-clock thresholds in package tests.
- Run the complete suite after each tracer-bullet change. Coverage percentage is supporting evidence, while every critical contract branch must have a direct behavioral test.
- The minimal-dependency release job sets `_R_CHECK_DEPENDS_ONLY_=true` and rebuilds examples, tests, and vignettes successfully with Suggested packages absent.
- The fully provisioned release matrix covers local data, live RSQLite, live DuckDB native and fallback execution, dtplyr, and Arrow. Optional backends may be conditional in generic jobs but must pass in at least one dedicated supported-platform job.
- Final verification runs linting, documentation generation, source-package build, CRAN-oriented checks from the tarball on R release/devel/oldrel, examples, vignettes, spelling, and a fresh two-axis code review plus Docs & Tests audit.
- The release gate is zero unresolved review findings, zero ERRORs and WARNINGs, and only understood/recorded CRAN NOTEs.

## Out of Scope

- New exported functions, arguments, grouping specifications, Parent-selection models, or presentation options.
- Parent shares for cubes or arbitrary Grouping sets.
- Percentage scaling, rounding, formatting, key completion, or subtotal-display policy.
- An Arrow query wrapper, message/status sentinel protocol, implicit Arrow collection, or broad Arrow method-preservation layer.
- Full Arrow Parent-share support until Arrow exposes a mechanism that preserves lazy scalar-cardinality validation, package condition classes, and user call context at an acceptably deep seam.
- Live execution against every simulated SQL dialect.
- A blanket subclass taxonomy for every error or conversion of rethrows and internal assertions.
- Treating every diagnostic string as permanent byte-for-byte public interface.
- Blanket snapshot coverage or tests of private helper implementation details.
- Refactoring unrelated backend materialization, making the Grouping plan opaque, or adding public adapter interfaces.
- A documentation-site visual redesign or new user-facing feature tutorial unrelated to the corrected contracts.
- Fixing disproved review claims such as missing outside-context Grouping-helper tests, missing zero-row integer `.id` tests, a functional factor-return bug, or a required custom printer removal.
- The CRAN upload itself; submission begins only after this spec's release gate and subsequent tickets are complete.

## Further Notes

- This spec follows the repository glossary and accepted ADRs 0002, 0005, 0006, 0007, 0009, 0010, 0014, and 0015.
- The implementation baseline is main commit `1c782eb3bf1579976a12dc5b7b4d203d41c81695`. ADR 0010 has accepted local amendments, and ADRs 0014 and 0015 are accepted additions awaiting inclusion with the work.
- Completed issues #7, #19, #20, and #21 provide the original lifecycle, Parent-share, backend, and documentation design. This spec is corrective hardening based on post-implementation review rather than a replacement feature design.
- A normal fully provisioned CRAN-oriented check passed with only the expected new-submission NOTE, while a dependency-only check reproduced three failures across examples, tests, and vignettes. A clean normal check therefore is not sufficient evidence for release.
- The prototype used dtplyr 1.3.3, data.table 1.18.4, Arrow 25.0.0, and rlang 1.3.0. It demonstrated the strict dtplyr expression-validator path and ruled out the investigated native Arrow hooks and a shallow wrapper design.
- The implementation should be split into blocker-aware tracer-bullet tickets before coding. Correctness and condition infrastructure precede adapter behavior that depends on them; documentation and final release verification follow stable behavior.
- Review completion means every finding has a visible disposition, not that every suggestion is implemented mechanically.
title: Harden marginplyr for its first CRAN release

## Observed

On a backend whose kind lacks `can_read_schema` (SQLite, Postgres — kinds `sql` and `postgres`), a `where()` predicate in a summary selection or in `.grouping` is refused with tidyselect's message and nothing else:

```r
summarize_with_margins(pg, across(where(is.numeric), sum), .grouping = rollup(region))
#> Error: This tidyselect interface doesn't support predicates.
summarize_with_margins(pg, n = n(), .grouping = rollup(where(is.character)))
#> Error: This tidyselect interface doesn't support predicates.
```

The same calls succeed on local data, dtplyr, DuckDB, and Arrow, because there the selection proxy carries column types.

## Why it is a finding

The refusal itself matches dbplyr: `summarize(pg, across(where(is.numeric), sum), .by = region)` is refused too. What differs is the Condition context. dplyr's own diagnostic reads

```
ℹ In argument: `across(where(is.numeric), sum)`
Caused by error in `across()`:
! This tidyselect interface doesn't support predicates.
```

while marginplyr's names neither the argument nor the verb, which is the context CONTEXT.md's *Condition context* entry says a Margin verb owes. The reason for the refusal — that this backend's proxy is the lazy table itself, per `grouping_selection_proxy()` in `R/backend-metadata.R`, because reading a schema would send a query (ADR 0020) — is also stated nowhere a caller reads.

## Proposed remedy

Catch the tidyselect refusal at `resolve_summary_selection()` and at the `.grouping` selection site, and re-raise it with the argument as the caller spelled it, the Margin verb as the blamed call, and a line saying that a predicate needs column types this backend does not expose without a query. Document the limit in *Relationship to dplyr summaries*.
title: where() on a backend with no readable schema is refused with a bare tidyselect diagnostic

## Status

**Implemented, reviewed, and corrected; ready to merge.** Branch
`sayuks/share-of-total` at `054444d`, nine commits on top of `main`
(`36987b3`): the four preparation commits, then the implementation
(`e5830fd`), the help page (`59ba220`), the tests and `proves` entries
(`35f0bb1`), the review corrections (`631d4c1`), the guides (`a0b789a`), and the test gaps (`054444d`).
No PR opened.

Local checks at that commit: `lintr::lint_package()` and
`spelling::spell_check_package()` clean, `roxygen2::roxygenise()` produces no
diff, the whole suite green with DuckDB, RSQLite, dtplyr, and Arrow installed,
`_R_CHECK_DEPENDS_ONLY_=true R CMD check` **Status: OK**, and
`altdoc::render_docs()` followed by `.github/scripts/verify-site.R` passing.

Decisions live in
`design/adr/0017-calculate-total-shares-against-the-grand-total-set.md` and
are not restated here.

## Problem

`share_of_parent()` answers "how much of its parent is this row?". The more
common reporting question is "how much of the whole is this row?", and
marginplyr cannot answer it on a lazy backend at all. Locally a caller has to
extract the root row by bit mask, hard-code the mask value, and divide — which
breaks under `.by`, since each partition needs its own denominator, and needs
a hand-written self-join on a database.

## Solution

`share_of_total()`, a second contextual summary helper with the same
signature as `share_of_parent()`, dividing by the Grand total set within each
fixed `.by` partition. Source contract, `across()` grammar, output naming,
value rules, and backend boundaries are ADR 0010's, unchanged.

## Remaining work

1. **Implementation.** Make the mapping construction and join-key set in
   `apply_joined_shares()` functions of the share kind, per ADR 0017's
   "Total shares get their own denominator mapping". The local `parent_ids`
   in that function becomes `target_ids` as part of this change; it was left
   alone in `21b20c5` deliberately so the rename would not precede the
   behaviour. Diagnostics and the Arrow rejection name the helper the caller
   actually wrote.
2. **Documentation.** One help page via `@rdname`, opening with the
   denominator comparison table. `roxygen2::roxygenise()` and commit `man/`.
   `NEWS.md`.
3. **Tests.** Contract tests and snapshots for Total shares, including the
   empty-`.by` denominator join, `cube()`, and `.duplicates = "keep"`.

## What CI will not catch

`verify-backend.R` fails a job when a test named in `proves` did not run. It
does not fail when a test exists but is not named there. Total-share contract
tests added without a matching `proves` entry in
`.github/workflows/release-matrix.yaml` will pass CI while proving nothing
about that backend. Each of the DuckDB, RSQLite, dtplyr, and Arrow jobs needs
its Total-share test names added.

## What was built

**Implementation (`e5830fd`).** Every request carries its *kind*, and one
table maps a kind to the name a caller writes, the terms its diagnostics use,
what it requires of the compiled plan, and the denominator it joins. The
mapping construction and join-key set in `apply_joined_shares()` are functions
of that kind, and its local `parent_ids` became `target_ids`. A Total share's
mapping is one read of the Grand total occurrence matched on the fixed keys;
without fixed keys a constant column stands in, which keeps that case on the
same missing-safe join as every other rather than adding a second join shape.
`execute_shares()` runs one adapter pass per requested kind, and each pass
overwrites the placeholder column its requests reserved in the caller's
written order, so a call requesting both kinds is not reordered by the passes.
The Arrow rejection and every diagnostic name the helpers the caller wrote.

**Documentation (`59ba220`).** One help page via `@rdname`, opening with the
denominator comparison table, with each section written for both helpers and a
helper named only where a rule is its own. The value rules state the two
duplicate-occurrence rules separately, as ADR 0017 requires: a Parent share
skips duplicate occurrences because a parent must be strictly less detailed,
while duplicate Grand total occurrences hold the same values and are
interchangeable. `NEWS.md` records the helper.

**Tests and release gates (`35f0bb1`).** Local contract tests for the plans a
Total share accepts and refuses, the empty-`.by` denominator join and the
internal name it allocates, `cube()`, `.duplicates = "keep"`, the value rules,
`across()`, and diagnostics naming the written helper; live backend contracts
for RSQLite, DuckDB, dtplyr, and Arrow. Each new backend contract is named in
its job's `proves` list, which is the thing above that CI would not have
caught on its own.

## Review

`/code-review` against `origin/main`, this issue as the Spec input. Four
findings, all resolved in `631d4c1`; one left as raised.

**A renamed help section broke the gate that reads the rendered site.**
`.github/scripts/verify-site.R` asserts markers in `docs/man/`, and three of
them named sections this branch renamed for both helpers — *Direct Parent
shares*, *Column-wise Parent shares*, and the summary verb's *Parent shares* —
so the `altdoc` workflow, which runs on every pull request, would have failed.
Its markers now name the sections that exist, and two of them state what the
rename was for: the page carries `share_of_total`, and it still says neither
helper completes keys. Checked by rendering the site and running the gate, not
by reading the Rd. The `proves` entries this issue did warn about were
correct.

**The help page described the Grand total set in the words the glossary lists
under _Avoid_.** `9840e04` added that entry, and ADR 0017 rejected
`share_of_root()` because "'root' is the word the glossary now lists under
Grand total set as one to avoid" — while the page the same branch rewrote
still said *root row*, *root share*, and *a root Parent share*. The prose and
the example variable now name the set. The rule is unchanged: the set with no
parent is the Grand total set.

**One kind was dispatched on in four places.** A vocabulary table, a terms
table, a grouping-requirement cascade, and a denominator rule each answered
for a kind separately, and the code comment conceded that a third helper would
have to be added to three of them. `share_kind_rules()` is now the one table,
and detection reads it backwards from a written name.
`share_grouping_spec_validator()` deliberately stays an asymmetry rather than
a table column: only a Parent share can be refused from the specification
alone, and a way to combine several specification validators would guard a
case that cannot arise.

**`grand_total_set_ids()` and `total_set_ids()` returned opposite shapes under
near-identical names.** The first is now `grand_total_occurrence_ids()`, named
for the occurrences it returns; the second keeps the name and shape of
`parent_set_ids()`, which is the interface the rule table reads.

One finding is left as raised. `share_output`, `source_summary`, and
`share_kind` travel together through the validators, which is a data clump.
They already travel as records where a record can go — the request, the share
pair, the cardinality record — and the three-string form survives only at the
boundary where a validator call is generated into a dtplyr expression and its
arguments must be literals. Two of the three are also condition fields, so
bundling them would change what a handler reads.

## Test sufficiency

The work was not written test-first: the order was implementation,
documentation, tests, as listed above. Sufficiency was therefore measured
rather than assumed, with `covr` over `R/share.R` and by mutating the module
in an isolated copy to see which tests fail.

Twelve mutations, ten killed. Two survive on purpose. Taking the denominator
from the last Grand total occurrence rather than the first changes no result,
which is ADR 0017's "which one a calculation uses as its denominator is not
specified" holding rather than a missing test. Dropping `na_matches = "na"`
from the non-SQL join also changes nothing: dplyr already defaults to it and
data.table matches missing keys inherently, so the argument states the intent
rather than causing the behaviour, and the SQL path spells the same rule out
in its own `ON` clause.

Three real gaps were found and closed in `054444d`: a plan whose every
occurrence is the Grand total set, which only a Total share can reach and
which joins nothing at all; empty input with a Total share, claimed for both
helpers by the value rules and tested for one; and `.unpack` and `.names`
written as names rather than literals, which reach a second check after
evaluation and predate the second helper.

`R/share.R` is at 95.9% line coverage. What remains uncovered is defensive:
unreachable duplicates of admission checks that the preflight pass rejects
first, `stop()` guards for kinds and backend kinds that no public call can
name, and empty-input rebranches of `names(dots)`.

## Open judgment calls

- `design/review-dispositions.md` cites `test-parent-share.R` and
  `check_parent_scalar()`, both renamed in `21b20c5`/`5e908ee`. It was left
  untouched because it is a ledger of the completed 0.1.0 review and
  rewriting names inside a finding would misreport what that review saw. Its
  citations therefore no longer resolve.
- `design/architecture.md` describes the module as owning "every Parent-share
  responsibility". That scope statement is still accurate today and needs
  updating as part of step 1. **Done in `e5830fd`**, together with the adapter
  signature, the mapping and calculation responsibilities, and the test seams;
  `631d4c1` updated it again for the consolidated rule table.
- The vignettes and `README.md` described Parent shares only, which was left
  out of the three Remaining work items above as guide-level work belonging to
  #82. **Reversed in `a0b789a`**: each guide now shows `share_of_total()`
  where it already answers the parent question — the README and Get started
  beside `share_of_parent()` and on the `cube()` a Parent share refuses,
  Grouping identity inside the example that is already about structural
  lookup, and Database and lazy backends as its rendered staged query.
  `verify-site.R` gained one marker per page. #82 still holds the recipes
  vignette.

## Prototype

`sayuks/proto-convenience-api` (`d17aaab`) carries a working prototype, but
ADR 0017 explicitly rejects its denominator mapping, which reuses the parent
union unchanged. Only its `share_helper_kinds` vocabulary and its approach to
resolving the denominator occurrence carry over.

Blocked by: #19

## Goal

Extend the Parent share stage to every supported lazy backend without
duplicating the value contract in native and portable adapters or executing a
query during `summarize_with_margins()`.

Specification baseline:

- commit [`aa6a1d9`](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/commit/aa6a1d9)
- [ADR 0010](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/aa6a1d9/design/adr/0010-compute-parent-shares-as-a-contextual-summary.md)

## Execution design

- Ordinary summaries run through the existing native or portable adapter.
- Preserve collision-safe internal Grouping set metadata through that result,
  even when the caller does not request `.id`.
- Add one common lazy Parent-share stage after ordinary Margin aggregation.
  Do not put separate parent-ratio implementations in the adapters.
- Build one shared parent mapping for all requested measures and skip
  identical duplicate occurrences while finding the next strictly coarser
  rollup set.
- Match fixed and included grouping keys with missing-safe identity. Do not
  rely on SQL `NULL = NULL` and do not join on displayed Margin labels.
- Batch multiple Parent shares through the shared mapping rather than adding
  one parent join per measure.
- Cast numerator and denominator explicitly so integer division cannot occur
  and output columns are double.
- Remove all internal metadata and restore the caller's requested column order
  before returning the lazy result.

## Laziness and error boundary

- `summarize_with_margins()` returns a lazy result for dbplyr, Arrow, and
  dtplyr inputs.
- Do not add an ordinary-summary schema or cardinality probe and do not
  collect solely to improve a Parent-share error.
- Statically detectable helper errors remain targeted before backend
  execution.
- When a general dbplyr backend cannot expose the arbitrary summary-result
  type or scalar cardinality without execution, an incompatible expression
  may fail with the database error at `collect()`. Document and test this
  boundary where simulation permits.
- The portable guarantee covers finite numeric values, `NA`/`NULL`, and zero
  denominators. Do not invent a cross-dialect `isfinite()` abstraction.

## Acceptance criteria

- Live DuckDB native execution agrees with the local implementation for
  direct, `across()`, multiple-measure, `.by`, missing-key, zero/missing
  denominator, root, and empty-input cases.
- PostgreSQL native SQL renders the required staged query through the dbplyr
  simulator.
- Generic and named fallback SQL simulators render a portable staged query
  without relying on native grouping sets or dialect-specific missing
  equality.
- Arrow and dtplyr retain supported lazy behavior and agree after collect.
- Parent-share computation does not add one aggregation or parent mapping per
  measure.
- Internal names cannot collide with adversarial source, summary, grouping,
  label, or `.id` names.
- Downstream `select()`, `filter()`, `arrange()`, `mutate()`, `show_query()`,
  and `collect()` compose with the staged lazy result.
- SQL tests assert semantic query shape rather than byte-for-byte formatting.
- Native and forced-portable DuckDB results agree.
- `devtools::test()` and `R CMD check` pass.

## Non-goals

- Do not execute every simulated SQL dialect against a live server.
- Do not expose parent joins, internal set identifiers, or staging options in
  the public interface.

## Summary

On DuckDB, `share_of_parent()` and `share_of_total()` compute a number from a
character source summary, with no diagnostic from either marginplyr or the
database. The same call on a local data frame is refused.

`?share_of_parent`'s *Lazy execution boundaries* states the contract this
breaks:

> The eligible-type rule is also enforced on every backend, and no backend
> calculates a share from a source it has shown to be ineligible.

and, for a dialect classified as refusing:

> Where it refuses an ineligible summary, that refusal is the answer and
> reaches you as the database's own diagnostic when `dplyr::collect()` executes
> the staged query.

Neither happens. This is the same class of defect as #106 (closed) on a
different dialect and through a different mechanism, so it is filed separately
rather than reopened.

## Reproduction

```r
pkgload::load_all(".", quiet = TRUE)
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))

df <- data.frame(a = c("x", "x", "y"), s = c("1", "2", "3"))
con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb())
tb <- copy_to(con, df, "d")

summarize_with_margins(
  tb, total = max(s), ps = share_of_parent(total), .grouping = rollup(a)
) |> collect()

summarize_with_margins(
  df, total = max(s), ps = share_of_parent(total), .grouping = rollup(a)
)
```

```
# DuckDB, with the default `.check_share_source = TRUE`:
      a total        ps
  1   x     2 0.6666667
  2   y     3 1.0000000
  3 Total   3 1.0000000

# local:
Error in `summarize_with_margins()`:
! Parent share `ps` requires source summary `total` to be a plain integer or
  double scalar.
i Detected type character.
```

## Root cause

`probe_share_dialect()` (`R/share.R:2371`) measures the dialect with
`sum("x", na.rm = TRUE)`. DuckDB refuses `SUM('x')`, so the verdict is
`"refuses"` and `check_dialect_share_sources()` (`R/share.R:2233`) returns
without a diagnostic, leaving the rule to the database.

But the staged share query never applies an aggregate to the source. It
compares it to `0.0` and divides two `as.double()` casts (`R/share.R:2646`),
which dbplyr renders for DuckDB as `TRY_CAST(... AS DOUBLE)`. DuckDB casts a
numeric-looking `VARCHAR` implicitly in the `= 0.0` comparison, and `TRY_CAST`
raises for nothing, so the share comes back a number.

What the probe measures and what the query depends on are two different dialect
behaviours. A non-numeric string such as `"n"` does raise on DuckDB, but only
incidentally, out of the `= 0.0` comparison's implicit cast, rather than from
any rule the package established.

## Why this is not `ready-for-agent`

The fix is a design decision, not a mechanical change, and the options differ
in what they cost under ADR 0020:

1. **Change what the probe measures** — ask the dialect about the operation the
   share query actually performs (`CAST` / comparison) rather than `SUM`. This
   keeps the two-query budget the ADR's second exemption allows but changes
   what "refuses" means, and may reclassify dialects already cached under the
   current question.
2. **Change the query** — make the staged share apply an operation the refusing
   dialects reject on a character source, so the refusal the contract promises
   is actually produced at `collect()`. This costs nothing in queries but adds
   an expression to every share on every dialect.
3. Reclassify DuckDB as `"converts"`, which refuses the share outright and is
   the safe reading, at the cost of refusing shares that work today.

Pick one before implementing; ADR 0020 and
`investigation/share-source-eligibility-on-coercing-dialects.md` are the
sources.

## What is unmeasured

- Which other dialects classified `"refuses"` share DuckDB's cast behaviour.
  Only DuckDB was measured; PostgreSQL and the generic `sql` kind were not.
- Whether `share_of_total()` differs from `share_of_parent()` here. Only the
  parent share was run.
title: DuckDB calculates a share from a character source the eligible-type rule should refuse

## Parent

#7

## What to build

Route `summarize_with_margins()` end to end through the shared Margin
operation lifecycle while preserving local summary semantics, native
`GROUPING SETS`, portable `UNION ALL`, grouping identity, and lazy query
composition.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add characterization coverage before changing any summary behavior or
      query-order contract that is not already protected.
- [ ] Capture summary expressions, `.by`, and `.grouping` exactly once at the
      public verb.
- [ ] Pass one opaque Margin operation to a dedicated summary executor rather
      than reading operation fields in the public verb.
- [ ] Resolve summary selections, infer output names, reserve internal names,
      and reject grouping-column overwrites before semantic margin-label
      validation.
- [ ] Reject invalid schema-aware summaries before an opt-in label collision
      query can contact a lazy backend.
- [ ] Reuse the operation's single typed metadata snapshot for grouping
      selections, `across()`, `pick()`, prototypes, and factor metadata.
- [ ] Keep native-versus-portable execution selection inside the summary
      executor.
- [ ] Preserve `grouping_bit()` and `grouping_id()` semantics for local,
      native SQL, and portable execution.
- [ ] Preserve local and dtplyr summary behavior, including column-wise and
      data-frame-valued summaries, dynamic names, context-helper rejection,
      duplicate policies, labels, factors, sorting, and ungrouped results.
- [ ] Preserve Arrow metadata and lazy summary behavior without executing the
      Arrow data query for schema discovery.
- [ ] Preserve live DuckDB native execution, PostgreSQL native rendering,
      fallback dialect rendering, identifier quoting, downstream subquery
      shape, and collection results.
- [ ] Do not require byte-for-byte SQL equality for non-semantic whitespace,
      aliases, parentheses, or collision-free internal suffixes.
- [ ] Pass focused summary tests and the complete testthat suite.

## Blocked by

- #8

body:
Charts the way from #318 — a plan written against a codebase that has since moved — to a settled specification.

## Destination

ADR 0027 is merged, and #318 is rewritten to the specification it settles. Each
of the four features #318 bundles has a decided verdict and a decided shape:

1. the `marginplyr_query_sql` condition signalled at the package's own query sites,
2. a `last_marginplyr_sql()` accessor reading back the last call,
3. `marginplyr.audit_sql_method = "explain"` as an alternative capture method,
4. `marginplyr.audit_sql_file` as an on-disk log.

A feature decided against is recorded in the ADR's *Considered options*, not
dropped silently. "Only 1 survives" is a legitimate answer this map can reach.

Writing the R code is not part of the destination.

## Notes

Domain: the marginplyr R package. Every session reads `CONTEXT.md`, `AGENTS.md`,
and the ADRs under `design/adr/` that its ticket touches. Invoke `/grilling` and
`/domain-modeling` on every ticket unless the ticket says otherwise.

- **ADR 0020 enumerates its exemptions rather than deriving them from a shape.**
  Do not silently adopt the reading that a caller who opted into `"explain"` has
  thereby *asked for* the query. Adding that interpretation is an amendment to
  ADR 0020 and has to be argued as one.
- **`R/share.R:2301` already holds a package-level environment**
  (`share_dialect_verdicts`). #318's claim that this package has no such pattern
  is false. The precedent's shape is the opposite of what #318 proposes: a cache
  that is never reset, against a log reset at the start of every call. It is
  also what a test of any audit feature has to empty first, the way
  `test-share-backends.R` already does.
- **No share-source check reads the caller's data.** #318's second signal site
  audits a mechanism that was removed; what replaced it sends one constant
  query per dialect, cached after it answers. Whether that deserves an audit
  record is #381's to decide, not a rename. (#378)
- **`dbplyr::last_sql()` already exists**, and dbplyr is an Import here, so it is
  never absent. Confirmed against the installed dbplyr 2.6.0: its body is
  `the$last_sql`, written by the single line `the$last_sql <- out` in
  `db_sql_render()` — the function `collect()`, `compute()`, `show_query()`, and
  `sql_render()` all funnel through. It is one slot, overwritten, carrying no
  context, no method, and no time, and marginplyr's own internal renders write
  to it too. Every ticket arguing that marginplyr should record SQL argues
  against this, not against nothing. (#380)
- **A term enters `CONTEXT.md` from the ticket that fixes it**, never from a
  ticket of its own — a rejected feature names nothing, so the glossary cannot
  be written ahead of the verdicts. **Sent query** is in as of #381, on branch
  `decide-381-sent-query` (`bce5aef`), and `context` is ruled out as a field
  name: `CONTEXT.md:230` defines *Condition context* and *Margin operation*
  lists `operation context` under `_Avoid_`. #383 amended the entry on
  `decide-383-sent-queries-accessor` (that branch plus one commit): its first
  sentence said *a Margin operation*, which `inspect_grouping()` is not.
- **There is no condition, and the record's shape is settled.** #381 rejected
  the condition, so nothing on this map may reintroduce `withCallingHandlers()`
  as the route to a record without reopening that ticket. #383 then fixed the
  whole reader: `last_sent_queries()`, a per-call `dplyr::tibble()` of
  `purpose` and `sql`, emptied at the top of **`prepare_grouping_plan()`** —
  not `prepare_margin_operation()`, which `inspect_grouping()` never reaches —
  and refusing rather than returning an unaccounted-for zero rows.
- **#318 is wrong in two measured places**, and ADR 0027 records both as
  corrections rather than silently fixing them: the reset function above, and
  "the accessor never errors", whose cited precedent `rlang::last_error()`
  errors when empty. (#383)
- **The `sql_render()` the record needs is not an execution entry point.**
  `lazy_execution_entry_points()` (`tests/testthat/test-query-policy.R:93`)
  lists neither it nor `show_query()`, so recording the result query moves none
  of those snapshots. (#383)
- **There is one capture method, so there is no method.** #382 rejected
  `"explain"` on two independent grounds — #383's `sql` column already gives a
  caller the route to a plan, and a capture that fails outright on BigQuery, SQL
  Server and SAP HANA, raises on every `simulate_*()` connection, and prints
  text varying with `getOption("width")` is not an audit record. So
  `marginplyr.audit_sql_method` does not exist, #383's conditional `method`
  column does not appear, and **ADR 0020 is not amended** — it gains one line in
  *Related decisions* and nothing else. The record's promise is that it holds
  the statement **as it was sent**; that all four are executable single
  statements is a fact about the sites, not a contract.
  `lazy_execution_entry_points()` gains `dplyr::explain` and
  `dbplyr::remote_query_plan`, both `subject_test = FALSE`, with no positive
  control — what they assert is that marginplyr does not call them. (#382)
- **There is no file log, and marginplyr raises no warning of its own.** #384
  rejected the on-disk log, so nothing on this map may reintroduce a sink the
  package writes. The no-warning half is documented twice — `?marginplyr` at
  `R/marginplyr-package.R:71` and `CONTEXT.md`'s *Package condition* entry — and
  the only `warning()` marginplyr calls (`R/conditions.R:341`) re-raises an
  External condition unchanged. A ticket proposing a warning is proposing an
  amendment to both. ADR 0021 does not reach a condition marginplyr authors:
  its scope is `summarize_margin_union()` and External conditions. (#384)
- **There is no SQL-detection predicate, and the classification is not repeated.**
  #386 rejected `is_sql_lazy_query()`: every recorded site runs after
  `grouping_backend()` has classified the input, so `grouping_backend()` returns
  `is_sql` as a field and the record remembers it per call at
  `R/grouping-plan.R:185`. No recorded site takes a backend argument, and
  `validate_margin_label()` and `check_observed_label_collision()` gain no
  parameter. A ticket proposing a second classifier over `tbl_lazy`,
  `dtplyr_step`, or `arrow_input_classes()` is proposing what
  `is_lazy_backend_input()` (`tests/testthat/test-query-policy.R:151`) already
  declined. A Sent query is **SQL**, so dtplyr and arrow take no row, and a
  `sql_render()` that raises takes a row with `sql = NA_character_` rather than
  no row (#384's axiom) or an error (#383 verdict 7). (#386)
- The tickets decide. The pull to start writing the code is the signal the map
  is finished.

## Decisions so far

<!-- one line per closed ticket -->

- [Decide the marginplyr_query_sql condition: whether, where, and what it promises](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/issues/381) — **marginplyr records the SQL it sends and does not signal it**: the condition is rejected (nothing was found it alone can do), all four sites are recorded including the constant dialect probe, only `"result"` is a promised purpose, the opt-in is the session option `marginplyr.audit_sql` — the package's first option, as this would have been its first non-error condition — and a query is promised to be recorded before it is sent. Measured: `dbplyr::last_sql()` after a Margin verb holds the schema proxy on duckdb, the label scan under `.check_margin_label`, and on RSQLite *a stale query about an unrelated table*, with nothing saying so.
- [Decide the "explain" capture method against ADR 0020](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/issues/382) — **rejected, on two grounds recorded independently** so that neither rests on the other: #383's `sql` column already reaches a plan without marginplyr mediating — the `"result"` query's lazy object is returned unexecuted, and the three internal statements are readable from the record — and #379 measured that the capture fails outright on BigQuery (GoogleSQL has no `EXPLAIN` statement), SQL Server and SAP HANA, raises on every `dbplyr::simulate_*()` connection so the suite largely cannot see it, prints text varying with `getOption("width")`, the caller's indexes and row counts, and DuckDB's `explain_output`, and fails *silently* under #318's `tryCatch`, contradicting #381's record-before-send. **ADR 0020 is therefore not amended**: no third exemption, and the opt-in is not read as the caller asking. Per-site application is refused too — the exemptions enumerate queries, not sites, so `EXPLAIN collect(head(.data, 0L))` needs one as much as the `"result"` site does. `marginplyr.audit_sql_method` and #383's `method` column go with it; `lazy_execution_entry_points()` gains `dplyr::explain` and `dbplyr::remote_query_plan`, moving one snapshot and taking no positive control, so the rejection is structural rather than prose.
- [Decide whether a caller reads back the last call's SQL, and from what](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/issues/383) — **`last_sent_queries()`**, an exported accessor over a per-call record: a `dplyr::tibble()` of `purpose` and `sql` (no `time`, no backend column; `method` only if #382 keeps `"explain"`), emptied at the top of **`prepare_grouping_plan()`** and not `prepare_margin_operation()` — measured: `inspect_grouping()` reaches `grouping_selection_proxy()` through the former only, so #318's placement would append its proxy query to the previous call's record. It **refuses** when nothing is recorded or the last call was not audited, returning zero rows only for an audited call that sent nothing; the option is read once at the reset and remembered, recording reads `isTRUE()` and reports nothing, a failed call's record is promised readable, the dialect probe's control gets its own row, and concurrency gets one documented sentence. `dplyr::tibble()` follows ADR 0013, which also forecloses a print method.
- [Re-identify #318's query sites and precedents against the current code](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/issues/378) — three signal sites survive (`finalize_margin_operation()` `R/margin-operation.R:332`, `grouping_selection_proxy()` `R/backend-metadata.R:13`, `check_observed_label_collision()` `R/margin-label.R:270`) and no site #318 missed was found; **#318's fourth has no subject** — no share-source checker reads the caller's data any more, and the only SQL left there is a constant, per-dialect-cached probe; the `is_sql_lazy_query()` extraction buys nothing and must call `arrow_input_classes()` rather than copy it; #318's body is corrected in place.
- [What does dplyr::explain() send, per backend?](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/issues/379) — the only method is `explain.tbl_sql`, so `explain()` **raises** on a `dbplyr::simulate_*()` connection and on a `dtplyr_step`; **GoogleSQL has no `EXPLAIN` statement**, so on BigQuery the cost question has no subject and the statement simply fails; `dbplyr::remote_query_plan()` returns the plan as a character vector, so `capture.output()` is not the only route; the plan text varies with `getOption("width")`, the caller's indexes and row counts, and DuckDB's `explain_output`; and dbplyr's default `EXPLAIN {sql}` is a **syntax error** on at least BigQuery, SQL Server outside Synapse dedicated pool, and SAP HANA.
- [What does session state cost an R package, and what shape are the last-call precedents?](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/issues/380) — nothing in CRAN policy or WRE forbids a package writing to an environment it owns; of eight last-call accessors across seven packages **none** has #318's shape (a log emptied at call start and appended to within the call), and `rlang::last_error()` — #318's sole cited precedent — errors when empty where #318 promises it never does; a package environment is invisible across fork/PSOCK/callr and no precedent documents a position on that.
- [Decide the on-disk audit log: whether, what format, and whose failure](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/issues/384) — **rejected, and rejected as incompatible rather than as worthless**: the honest form is write-or-stop, since a record whose purpose is completeness must not silently acquire a hole, and that contradicts #383 verdict 7 — a bad option value must not turn `summarize_with_margins()` into an error; #318's form avoids the contradiction by warning and continuing, which *is* the hole, and buys it with the package's first warning of its own against a sentence documented twice (`R/marginplyr-package.R:71` and `CONTEXT.md`'s *Package condition*). The explicit `write_sent_queries(path)` writer is rejected **separately**, because that argument does not reach it: it is one export over `utils::write.csv(last_sent_queries(), path)` and still fixes a format the package then owns — **holding no format is the feature**, since no one format answers an auditor, and #318's `----` block is unparseable when its own payload carries the separator (SQL's line comment is `--`). `time` does not return, #318's throttle question dissolves with a correction — ADR 0021's scope is `summarize_margin_union()` and External conditions, so it never reached — and `last_sent_queries()`'s Rd carries the append recipe instead. ADR 0027 records the rejection **conditionally**, naming #383 verdict 7 and the no-warning axiom as what would have to change.
- [Decide whether the record needs a SQL-detection predicate](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/issues/386) — **no predicate**: #318's warrant was an argument about the helper #381 removed, and #383's reset in `prepare_grouping_plan()` puts every recorded site after `grouping_backend()` has run. `grouping_backend()` returns **`is_sql`** as a field — already a local at `R/grouping-backend.R:14`, and measured across eight shapes to agree exactly with `!is.null(backend$dialect)`, including the two that could have broken it (`sql_dialect.default` is `function(con) con`, and `lazy_frame(con = NULL)` still builds a `TestConnection`) — rejecting the dialect-nullity spelling for naming something other than what it decides and a `kind %in%` set for being a second place to keep in step. The record **remembers** it per call at `R/grouping-plan.R:185`, #383 verdict 6's move a second time, so no signature changes and no label checker learns about backends. The input's backend answers for the **result**, which the lazy-execution-boundaries contract already settles. The dialect probe's two rows are **SQL by construction** and get no runtime test. A Sent query is SQL, so dtplyr and arrow take no row and the Rd says the record promises the SQL sent, not the execution caused. Measured: `sql_render()` passes unknown functions through (`weird_udf`, `strsplit`, `match` all render) but raises on an explicitly refused translation, and raises at **render**, not build — which bites only at `"result"` and the probe, since the other two sites `collect()` the same query a moment later; that case takes a row with `sql = NA_character_`, satisfying #384's completeness axiom and #383 verdict 7 at once. ADR 0027 records the rejection under the general rule it rests on.

- [Write ADR 0027 and rewrite #318 to the settled specification](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/issues/385) — the assembly step, decided nothing: [ADR 0027](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/main/design/adr/0027-record-the-sql-marginplyr-sends.md) is merged (`130a1a3`), holding the surviving feature and every rejection in *Considered options*; ADR 0020 gained one *Related decisions* line and **no amendment**; the two research notes came onto `main` so the ADR's *Evidence* resolves; `CONTEXT.md` needed nothing, **Sent query** already carrying it; and #318 is rewritten and retitled to the specification, with a *What is not built* list so it is not read as a subset of the older plan. The review corrected this map as well as the branch: `prepare_grouping_plan()` is **not** the common ancestor of the recorded sites — only the selection proxy is inside it, the observed-label scan and the dialect probe being reached from siblings of its own caller. What decides the reset placement is that all five entry points reach it and that it runs before every one of the four sites on every path to them.

## Not yet specified

<!-- empty: the map is complete -->

Nothing. The way to the destination is walked. The docs patch — what the `R/marginplyr-package.R` and
`vignettes/database_backends.qmd` sections have to say — waited on #384 alone
and is fully determined by the closed tickets, so it is part of the #318 rewrite
[#385](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/issues/385) assembles rather than a
decision of its own. The `is_sql_lazy_query()` patch graduated into
[Decide whether the record needs a SQL-detection predicate](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/issues/386),
now closed, so #385 is unblocked and is the only ticket left on this map.

## Out of scope

- Implementing the feature — the R code, the tests, the vignette prose, the
  roxygen. This map produces the decision; the build is a separate effort.
- A remote log sink, a rotation or retention policy, and a structured (JSON/CSV)
  on-disk format. #318's own scope call, carried forward.
- Changing what the share-eligibility probe or the observed-label-collision
  check *do*. This effort only decides what is recorded about them.

Note: a per-entry-point `.audit_sql` argument is **not** out of scope — it is a
rejected alternative, and belongs in the condition ticket's considered options.
title: Map: recording the SQL marginplyr sends
